title: Match the Energy
pin_title: ADHD Tasks: Match Difficulty to Current Energy
description: ADHD energy is not constant. On a low day, choose the smallest possible version of the task instead of forcing the full version. High-energy windows are for harder steps. Matching the size of the step to how you feel right now prevents shutdown and keeps momentum possible. #ADHD #Energy #ADHDTips #Focus

title: Leave a Note
pin_title: ADHD Memory: Use External Reminders Instead of Hoping
description: Relying on memory alone is hard with ADHD. Write the next step on a sticky note and put it where you will see it. The note becomes the reminder so your brain does not have to hold the plan. Seeing the step makes starting easier than trying to remember it. #ADHD #Reminders #ADHDTips #ExecutiveFunction
scene_prompt: A small sticky note with a tiny star stuck to a laptop lid, soft morning light, everything fully visible and brightly lit

title: Stop When Ready
pin_title: ADHD Work: Give Yourself Permission to Stop
description: Many ADHD sessions end in guilt because stopping feels like failure. Set a short timer and stop when it ends, even if you could do more. Stopping on purpose trains your brain that starting is safe because you control the exit. Short complete sessions build more trust than long unfinished ones. #ADHD #Timer #ADHDTips #SelfCompassion

title: See the Win
description: ADHD brains need clear signals that something happened. After a small step, mark it in a way you can see: a check, a star, a moved object. Visible progress reduces the feeling that nothing is moving and makes the next start feel more possible. One mark is enough. #ADHD #Progress #ADHDTips #Focus
scene_prompt: A wooden board with three soft glowing stars, one newly lit, warm afternoon light, everything fully visible and brightly lit

title: Open the File
pin_title: ADHD Start: Open the File and Nothing More
description: The hardest part is often just opening the thing. Make the first action only opening the document or the app, then stop if you want. Once it is open, the next sentence is usually easier. Starting with the tiniest visible action lowers the barrier without requiring motivation first. #ADHD #Starting #ADHDTips #Focus
